name: Hamstring stretch on a step
why: Stretches the back of the thigh, which tightens with running and sitting.
setup: Stand facing a low step, bench or rock and rest one heel on it, leg straight, toes pointing up.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach further
feel: A stretch in the back of the thigh.
stopIf: Tingling or pain down the leg: that's a nerve, not a muscle, so ease off.

name: Standing quad stretch
why: Stretches the front of the thigh after running, cycling or hiking downhill.
setup: Stand tall holding a wall or tree for balance.
cues: Bring your heel towards your bottom
mistakes: Letting the knee drift forward or out
feel: A stretch along the front of the thigh.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
why: Lowering yourself slowly from kneeling builds hamstring strength in the lengthened position, which strongly reduces hamstring strains and is part of sport injury-prevention programmes.
setup: Kneel on a mat with your heels anchored under a sofa or held by a partner.
Body straight from knees to head, arms ready to catch you.
cues: Lower forward as slowly as you can
mistakes: Too many reps too soon (very sore legs)
feel: Very hard work in the back of the thighs.
stopIf: Sharp pain in the back of the thigh.
cautions: Start with 1-2 sets of 3-5: soreness for 2-3 days is normal at first.
